concept: Search index-time versus query-time analyzer compatibility
summary: Source-anchored research for Search index-time versus query-time analyzer compatibility. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Compatibility requires aligned term normalization, even when token boundaries appear suitable. OpenSearch documents a query override that produces lowercase jo while indexed prefix terms contain Jo, yielding no hits. Elastic’s matching explanation likewise depends on exact equality of normalized query and indexed terms. This is mechanism evidence, not a claim that MongoDB implements OpenSearch query overrides. (high confidence)

For cross-product graph analysis, OpenSearch documents that indexing ignores positionLength while graph-aware query processing can use it. Elasticsearch demonstrates phrase false positives and false negatives from lost graph structure, warns that flattening loses information, and recommends graph filters at search time where possible. These sources justify checking phrase behavior as well as token strings; they do not establish MongoDB graph-query controls. (medium confidence)

MongoDB Search explicitly prohibits wordDelimiterGraph in the searchAnalyzer when querying with regex or wildcard because it produces multiple output tokens per input token. The documented remedy is to specify a different searchAnalyzer. Do not generalize this operator-specific prohibition to all full-text queries. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Recommended test procedure, synthesized from the sources: inspect document-side and query-side token output, then run expected-hit and expected-miss queries against the chosen pair. Include case or accent variants relevant to normalization, a longer-prefix negative case when indexing expands tokens, and phrase tests when graphs are involved. Elastic explicitly recommends testing separate search analyzers before production; token inspection alone does not validate query semantics. (medium confidence)

Elasticsearch documents a concrete precision failure when the prefix-expanding index analyzer is also used for searching: indexing Apple yields a, ap, app, appl, apple, while querying appli yields overlapping short prefixes and can incorrectly match Apple. A search analyzer emitting only appli removes that accidental overlap. This example establishes a reason for asymmetry; it does not prove MongoDB text-operator behavior for every match criterion. (high confidence)

With MongoDB wildcard and allowAnalyzedField: true, character and token filters still apply, but tokenization is skipped and the query output remains one token. Thus foo bar* cannot match foo bar baz indexed as separate foo, bar and baz terms: no indexed term starts with foo bar. Changing the search analyzer cannot reconstruct an original multiword term that indexing split apart. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents flattenGraph after wordDelimiterGraph to make that graph-producing output suitable for indexing. This MongoDB-specific indexing instruction does not establish that every MongoDB query operator preserves token graphs. (low confidence)

MongoDB’s documented email pair keeps the same @-to-AT character mapping and whitespace tokenization on both sides, but adds shingles and edgeGram only at index time. It is a concrete compatibility pattern: preserve the shared normalization and boundary rules while omitting index expansion from query analysis. (low confidence)

The MongoDB standard- and keyword-analyzer documentation describes Atlas Visual Editor preview under Refine Your Index, Index Configurations and View text analysis. It shows index and search tokens for built-in sample document and query strings. Those pages document the preview for their named analyzers; they do not establish arbitrary custom-pair test coverage. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Elasticsearch’s analyze API accepts named custom analyzers on a specified index and returns terms, positions and offsets. This documents an Elasticsearch inspection tool, not an executed Atlas integration test or proof of an Atlas API. (low confidence)
